passportValidity.text: The UK Foreign Office says your passport must expire at least 90 days after the date you arrive in Lesotho and have at least 4 blank pages, because Lesotho border control stamps it and so does South African border control on the way to and from Lesotho.

travelInsurance.text: Visa applicants must submit proof of medical insurance with the application, according to the Home Affairs service charter. No official source we could read states whether visa-free visitors need it.

onwardTicket.text: Visitor visa applicants must include a return ticket with their application, according to the Home Affairs service charter. No official source states an onward-ticket check for visa-exempt visitors.

proofOfFunds.text: Tourist visa applicants must submit three months of bank statements or a valid debit or credit card with enough funds for the stay; visitors invited by a sponsor show statements of at least M10,000. No amount is published for visa-free arrivals.

source.name: Government of Lesotho — Service charter: Issuance of entry visa

currencyLimits.text: The UK Foreign Office says you must declare cash or travellers cheques in any currency worth 25,000 maloti or more, or the money could be seized when you leave and you could be fined. It says the loti is pegged 1:1 to the South African rand, and both are accepted throughout Lesotho.

source.name: UK Foreign Office — Lesotho entry requirements

notes: The UK Foreign Office says there are strict rules on goods you can take into or out of Lesotho, and you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

payments.text: The UK Foreign Office says the loti is pegged one-to-one to the South African rand and both are accepted throughout Lesotho, and that UK cards are widely accepted, but to take enough cash outside Maseru. Canada's travel advice says major credit cards are accepted only at major tourist establishments and banks.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says foreigners are vulnerable to opportunistic street and vehicle crime, including mugging and armed carjacking, with the danger greatest in urban areas, and advises not walking alone in isolated areas or after dark. It says driving standards and road conditions are poor and that animals on the roads are a hazard, especially at night.

bestTimeToVisit.text: Canada's travel advice says to expect extreme cold and heavy snowfall in the mountains from June to August, which can close roads and passes, and violent thunderstorms from November to February. The months shown are those outside both periods; no official source we could read recommends a time to visit.

idp.text: Lesotho is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Lesotho is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Lesotho yet.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says mountain weather can change rapidly and it can turn cold unexpectedly even in summer; from June to August it says to expect extreme cold and heavy snow, which can close roads and passes, and it advises carrying a blanket, warm clothes and a flashlight in mountain areas.
Canada's travel advice says you must have a four-wheel-drive vehicle to enter or leave Lesotho through the Sani Pass, and may need one for rural mountain areas reached only by dirt roads.
The UK Foreign Office says the loti is pegged one-to-one to the South African rand and both currencies are accepted throughout Lesotho.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Lesotho?
faq.answer: Citizens of SADC countries and of a list of Commonwealth and Western European states — including the US, UK, Ireland and Germany — enter Lesotho visa-free. The UK Foreign Office says British visitors can stay up to 90 days without a visa; Canada's travel advice says Canadians can stay up to 30 days. Other nationalities need a visa before travel.

faq.question: Can I visit Lesotho on a day trip from South Africa?
faq.answer: Yes, by road. The UK Foreign Office says all visitors to Lesotho travel through South Africa and must meet South Africa's entry requirements, and that both Lesotho and South African border control stamp your passport. Canada's travel advice says you must have a four-wheel-drive vehicle to use the Sani Pass crossing.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Lesotho?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK Foreign Office says you can extend your stay by completing a 90-day temporary permit extension form and taking it to the Visa Application Centre in the Manthabiseng Convention Centre, Maseru; your passport must be valid for the extension period, and if you overstay without permission the authorities may detain you and will charge weekly fines.

faq.question: Can I still apply for a Lesotho visa online?
faq.answer: No official source we could read offers a working online visa application for Lesotho. The Home Affairs service charter lists the documents required for an entry visa.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Lesotho?
faq.answer: Lesotho itself does not require one (WHO). South Africa, which the UK Foreign Office says all visitors to Lesotho travel through, requires a certificate from travellers aged 1 or over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission or after more than 12 hours' transit through an airport in one.
